Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <92qmn4$d5i$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,

spin...@my-deja.com wrote:
> every time i try to go there, it gives me a blank window, and
> freezes my machine. i'd really like to be able to check there

No idea about the problem with your system, but the complete errata,
rulings, and clarifications file is backed up here:

http://lasombra.tripod.com/cerc121500.htm

For use when you are having trouble accessing White Wolf's site.

> recent rule ???'s:
> 1. as i try to leave torpor with iliana (and she has 6 blood still on
> her,) the miscreant dimple blocks me. can i play kiss of ra?

Yes.
Kiss of Ra can be played by an acting vampire in torpor. [LSJ 19970325]

Dimple does not block you, he attempts to block you.
You then play the Kiss of Ra, and the Kiss of Ra blocks the action.

> does dimp go to torp?

Yes.
If he hasn't gained a fortitude skill card somewhere along the way.

> does he also get the chance to diablerize iliana?

This would say no,
Only ready vampires can commit diablerie. Vampires in Torpor cannot.
[RTR 19980623]

Also, the Kiss of Ra blocks the action, Dimple does not,
so Dimple has no opportunity to commit diablerie.

See LSJ's discussion of blocking & Kiss of Ra, here:
http://www.deja.com/getdoc.xp?AN=694133547
http://www.deja.com/getdoc.xp?AN=660751578
http://www.deja.com/getdoc.xp?AN=622531166
http://www.deja.com/getdoc.xp?AN=704688016
http://www.deja.com/getdoc.xp?AN=694136839

> 2. iliana wants to do rutor's hand action. the 1 point can't be
> prevented. can it be changed via skin of night to non-aggravated?

No.
Skin of Night is a combat card, and as such can only be played
in combat. If Iliana had a Heart of Darkness card, she could
treat the damage as normal damage rather than aggravated,
but she still couldn't prevent the damage.

> i guess no, because skin of night specifically says in a "combat
> round," but i wondered, since i thought there were weird errata
> about when damage prevention/alteration cards can be played.

Combat cards can only be played in combat.
Or as about to leave combat (ie Psyche, Telepathic Tracking).

The only card that lets you prevent damage outside of combat
is Blood Tears of Kephran, but even it will not let you prevent
the damage from Rutor's Hand.

Carpe Noctem.

Messages.Body:
spin...@my-deja.com wrote:
> The Lasombra <TheLa...@hotmail.com> wrote:

> > spin...@my-deja.com wrote:
> > > i guess no, because skin of night specifically says in a "combat
> > > round," but i wondered, since i thought there were weird errata
> > > about when damage prevention/alteration cards can be played.
> > Combat cards can only be played in combat.
> when did this re-happen? for a while, as i understood it, damage
> prevention was allowed whenever damage occurred, as long as the card
> text didn't say (cf. skin of steel) "damage from a strike/from
> strikes/this combat round." skin of rock, et al., could prevent
> incidental damage, such as can be incurred during an action.
> tell me if i'm wrong and this was never the case. (obviously, this
> contradicts the rule about combat cards being used only in combat,
> but as i say, i thought that was in the rulings at some point.)

This was never the case. The ruling you're thinking of is from
RTR 28-JUN-1998:

Damage Prevention cards: are not restricted to strike resolution.
#
# Combat cards can be played whenever appropriate during combat - and
# any time preventable damage is inflicted is an appropriate time for
# damage prevention.

> > Or as about to leave combat (ie Psyche, Telepathic Tracking).

Superior Psyche! is played after combat.
Superior Telepathic Tracking is played when combat is about to end.
